notes: TBox contraction, paired with the revision biology-replace-0005 ("Every spider has six legs") and removing the revision's original rule. The rule (every spider has eight legs) is stored very often and has no species-level exception. After the removal the model is meant to say it does not know how many legs a spider has. The three derived queries are the revision's: little-known spiders whose membership the prompt states (inheritance, 2 hops); nobody writes the leg count of these species by name, so the removed rule is the only route and the answer becomes "I don't know". The third is an application (a model's leg count), asked open. Well-known spiders (tarantula, black widow) are not asked, since a model may store their leg count by name. Residual risk, recorded: a model that knows spiders are arachnids may still reach eight through the arachnid rule; that is a patch, not a deletion of the spider rule. The negation is worded "Is it true that spiders do not have eight legs?" (no, then unknown); the conjunction side fact (spiders spin silk) is true and the disjunction side fact (spiders are mammals) is false, as under strong Kleene logic the three answers become unknown. Near unrelated: the eye count of spiders (eight), a neighbouring fact the removal must leave alone; contraction is exempt from the rule that its reference differs from the old answer.
